taxonomyNote: NatureServe: elevated to species by Douglas et al. (2007).
behavior: Generally solitary in summer; may congregate at favourable hibernation dens (NatureServe).
Diurnal in spring and fall, active mainly at dusk and at night in summer; in the north most activity is April-October (NatureServe).
Eats lizards, birds and mammals up to the size of woodrats and ground squirrels; lizards seem most important for juveniles (NatureServe).
habitat: Canyons, foothills, buttes and erosion gullies of rocky desert; sometimes sandy arroyos or desert flats with shrubs and burrows for cover; vegetation may include pinyon-juniper (NatureServe).
When inactive it occurs under rocks or bushes or in crevices, caves, abandoned mines or animal burrows (NatureServe).
range: Part of southern California (not the southernmost part) and adjacent southwestern Nevada (NatureServe); overlaps the southwestern speckled rattlesnake in parts of the Las Vegas Valley (NDOW).
